fact: A Request for Expressions of Interest, published 11 November 2025 by the Ministry of Communications and Technology, seeks a consultant firm to renew the existing National ICT Policy and Strategy (2019-2024) as a 2025-2029 policy, over about four months.
The notice describes the existing National ICT Policy and Strategy as covering 2019-2024, to be renewed for 2025-2029.
The renewal consultancy is paid from an IDA (World Bank) grant to Somalia under the Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP), per the notice.
The Ministry launched procurement of consultants to renew the ICT policy and strategy, with expressions of interest due 29 November 2025.

The article says the 2025-2030 strategy builds on the National ICT Policy and Strategy 2019-2024 (per the corroboration paragraph, We Are Tech Africa, 16 October 2025); dated by the article's publication, 2025-10-13.

fact: The article says officials cite the ICT Policy and Strategy (2019-2024) as backing the Starlink rollout, giving the policy's period as 2019 to 2024; the article is the 2025-09-24 publication date, which is used as the date.

Communications Minister Mohamed Adan Moalim said the Starlink launch supports the goals of the National ICT Policy and Strategy (2019-2024), which the article describes as aiming to expand digital access and strengthen domestic infrastructure.

The Digital Inclusion Policy states the National ICT Policy and Strategy (2019-2024) was developed by the Ministry of Communications and Technology, giving its period as 2019 to 2024; the document prints no date, so its published date 2025-08 is used.
The strategy states that the Ministry prepared a new five-year ICT Policy, which the Cabinet adopted on 28 November 2019.
The strategy names the Somalia National ICT Policy & Strategy as covering 2019-2024 (one passage elsewhere in it gives 2019-2023), with e-government as one of six priority areas.

The Ministry of Post, Telecommunications and Technology published the full National ICT Policy & Strategy 2019-2024 as a PDF on its own site (moct.gov.so); no date of the event is given, so the published date 2019-11 is used.

The document describes itself as the 5-year 2019-2024 National ICT Policy and Strategy covering the whole sector (access, infrastructure, regulation, cyber-security, skills, e-commerce, digital services, postal); no event date is given, so the published date 2019-11 is used.

The policy sets a table of actions and targets by area, each with a year of delivery (Year 1 to Year 5), and says estimated cost for each line is still to be determined by the relevant agencies; no costs are stated (date: published 2019-11).

The policy states that the Ministry of Post, Telecommunications and Technology sets the sector's policy agenda and heads the sector, and that the National Communications Authority, created by the 2018 Telecom Act, implements the federal government's policy (date: published 2019-11).

The policy lists national budget, development assistance, private sector and the NCA budget only as potential resources per action area and ties no budget line or amount to the policy (date: published 2019-11).

The World Bank states that in 2019 the Ministry of Communications and Technology (then Post, Telecommunications and Technology) adopted Somalia's first cross-cutting National ICT Policy and Strategy, with ITU and World Bank support.
The World Bank gives the policy's period as 2019-2024.
The World Bank reproduces the policy's goals and timelines, for example secondary-school ICT access by Year 3 and ICT courses in all secondary schools by Year 4, with no cost stated.

The Minister of Communications and Technology told the WSIS+20 forum on 9 July 2025 that the National ICT Policy was approved by the Council of Ministers earlier in 2025; no month is given, so the year is used.
SONSA Platform's policy brief evaluates Somalia's current National ICT Policy and Strategy (2019-2024).
SONSA Platform's brief gives the National ICT Policy and Strategy as covering 2019-2024 and calls for a revised strategy for 2025-2030.
